question:
A manufacturer produces products $A$ and $B$. Each unit of $A$ requires $2$ units of resource I and $1$ unit of resource II, while each unit of $B$ requires $1$ unit of resource I and $2$ units of resource II. At most $12$ units of each resource are available. The profit per unit is ₹300 for $A$ and ₹400 for $B$. Let $x$ and $y$ be the numbers of units produced.
(i) Write the constraints and the profit function.
(ii) Check whether $(5,4)$ is feasible.
(iii) If the feasible corner points are $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, $(4,4)$ and $(0,6)$, determine the optimal feasible solution.

options.A:
(i) $2x+y\leq12$, $x+2y\leq12$, $x,y\geq0$; maximise $Z=300x+400y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is feasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(4,4)$ with profit ₹$2800$
options.B:
(i) $2x+y\leq12$, $x+2y\leq12$, $x,y\geq0$; maximise $Z=300x+400y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is infeasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(4,4)$ with profit ₹$2800$
options.C:
(i) $x+2y\leq12$, $2x+y\leq12$, $x,y\geq0$; minimise $Z=300x+400y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is infeasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(0,6)$ with profit ₹$2400$
options.D:
(i) $2x+y\geq12$, $x+2y\geq12$, $x,y\geq0$; maximise $Z=400x+300y$
(ii) $(5,4)$ is feasible
(iii) Optimal solution $(6,0)$ with profit ₹$2400$
